chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Ash'ari, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Abu Salma, from Muhammad ibn Saeed ibn Ghazwan, from Muhammad ibn Bunan, from Abu Maryam, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

My father said one day, while his companions were with him: 'Which one of you is pleased to take a burning ember in his hand and hold it until it extinguishes?' He said: 'All the people were silent and hesitated, so I stood up and said: O my father, do you command me to do it?' He said: 'I did not mean you specifically; you are from me and I am from you, but rather I meant them.'

He said: 'And he repeated it three times, then said: 'How abundant is description (talk) and how scarce is action. Indeed, the people of action are few. Indeed, the people of action are few. Know that we recognize both the people of action and the people of description, and this was not pretense of ignorance from us towards you, but rather to test your news and record your impressions.'

He said: 'By Allah, it was as if the earth had sunk beneath them out of shame from what he had said, to the extent that I looked at one of them sweating profusely, not raising his eyes from the ground.' So when he saw that from them, he said: 'May Allah have mercy on you, for I did not intend except good. Indeed, Paradise has levels, so the level of the people of action cannot be reached by anyone from the people of speech, and the level of the people of speech cannot be reached by others.'
He said: 'By Allah, it was as if they had been released from their chains.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the people of action and the people of speech in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) tests his companions' readiness for true spiritual action by asking who will hold a burning ember, revealing the scarcity of those who embody their words. He clarifies that his question was a deliberate test to distinguish between mere description and actual practice, emphasizing that the rank of 'doers' is inaccessible to 'talkers' and vice versa. This hadith underscores the Shia emphasis on *amal* (action) over *qawl* (speech), illustrating how divine testing reveals the sincerity of the faithful.

en.hubeali: H 14737 – Al-Husayn Bin Muhammad Al-Ashary, from Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Saeed, from Muhammad Bin Muslim Bin Abu Salma, from Muhammad Bin Saeed Bin Gazwaan, from Muhammad bin Bunaan, from Abu Maryam, who has narrated the following:

Abu Ja’farasws says that one day myasws fatherasws said in the presence of hisasws companions: ‘Which one of you is good enough to hold a burning ember in his hand and extinguish it by squeezing it?’ All the people were silent and stressed out. So Iasws stood up and said: ‘O fatherasws! Do youasws command measws to do it?’ So heasws said: ‘It is not youasws Iasws meant, but rather, youasws are from measws and Iasws am from youasws, but it is they that Iasws have intended by it’.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And he<sup>asws</sup> repeated it thrice, then said: ‘How much is the description (talk) and how little the action. The people of action are few indeed. And we<sup>asws</sup> recognise the people of action and the description (talk) both, and this was only a pretence of blindness from us<sup>asws</sup> towards you. But, your news reaches us<sup>asws</sup> and we<sup>asws</sup> write down your impressions’.

Then he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! It is as if the earth has shaken them with the shame from what he<sup>asws</sup> had said to the extent that I<sup>asws</sup> looked at a man from among them sweating profusely and he was not raising his head from the ground’. So when he<sup>asws</sup> saw that (situation) among them, he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you all, for I<sup>asws</sup> have not intended except the good. In the Paradise there are Levels, so the level of the people of action cannot be understood by anyone from the people of the talk. And the Level of the people of the talk cannot be understood by others’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, it was as if they had been released from the chains’.
